text.p: Here are highlights of stories reported by Hungary's press, based on information by Nepszabadsag's Hungary Around the Clock service. For further details on how to subscribe to Hungary Around the Clock, please contact Monica Kovacs at (361) 351 2440 or fax your request to (361) 351 7141.
ALL PAPERS

- A delegation of six IMF directors yesterday wound up a three-day visit to Hungary. IMF director Bernd Esdar praised Hungary's exports, privatisation and the level of foreign investment and forecast other "positive signs", such as a faster GDP growth.
- The cabinet is expected today to debate a planned amendment to the public finance act, as well as trends in price changes next year, among other topics.

- Keynote speakers of the opposition expressed doubts Wednesday about whether the cabinet's targets would be implemented in next year's budget, while pro-government MPs considered the bill well-founded.

- The national presidential board of the Socialist Party and the body of executives of junior coalition partners the Free Democrats are due to hold a joint meeting in the near future to discuss coalition cooperation.

- Parliament's constitutional committee endorsed a report Wednesday on hearings regarding the HUF 804 million commission paid out by the State Privatistion and Holding Co. (APV) to lawyer Marta Tocsik over municipal land deals.
- Outgoing managing director of APV Istvan Kocsis, recently dismissed by the government, will continue to work at the company as a deputy CEO, said APV Chairman Arpad Kovacs.
- Police say that differences of opinion between criminal organisations specialising in the collection of extortion money may lie behind a number of explosions in Budapest recently.
MAGYAR HIRLAP

- The Young Democrats have caught up with the Socialist Party in popularity (15 per cent), closely followed by the Independent Smallholders' Party (14 per cent), according to a survey. The Free Democrats would pick up 7 per cent of the vote, and the Democratic Forum and the Christian Democrats 5 per cent each.
- Since January 1, the trading volume on the Budapest Commodity Exchange reached HUF 600 billion. The entire 1995 volume came to HUF 170 billion.
- The number of economic enterprises operating in Hungary increased in the third quarter by over 21,000 - or 3 per cent - according to a fresh report released by the Central Statistical Office.
- The number of the refrigeration company Goldsun Rt.'s employees will be cut from 320 to 150 - according to CEO Avi Roman Kamrat.
MAGYAR NEMZET
- This paper and Napi Gazdasag deal with foreign reactions to the resignation of National Bank vice presidents.
NAPI GAZDASAG
- The pharmaceutical company Richter has begun sale of an original new medicine named Curiosin, which helps the healing of scars.
- Budapest City Council will sell a further 8 per cent stake of the Budapest gas works Fogaz to the German firms VEW and Ruhrgas for HUF 2.58 billion.
VILAGGAZDASAG
- The domestic revenue of the pharmaceutical firm Egis is expected to be HUF 9 billion in the first ten months of 1996 and that of exports $56 million, said CEO Istvan Orban.
